title: Instance-unique layoutId for SubTabNavigation and SegmentedControl
body:
## Summary
SubTabNavigation and SegmentedControl hard-code one global framer-motion layoutId, so every instance on screen shares one highlight identity.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_shared/tabs.tsx:136 uses layoutId="activeSubTabBg" and src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_shared/navigation.tsx:147 uses layoutId="segmentedControlBg". 21 files import SubTabNavigation. When two strips are mounted together, framer treats both highlights as one shared-layout element: switching one strip can animate the pill out of the other or relegate it. Fixed: useId() per instance (or a LayoutGroup id), so each strip owns its highlight.

## Flow
- mount two SubTabNavigation instances on one page
- click a tab in the second strip
- predicted: the first strip's active pill animates toward, or is hidden by, the second

## Expected impact
Anyone switching tabs on a page with two strips sees each highlight stay put. Risk: a cross-strip animation someone relies on would stop (none found).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each tab strip keeps its own active highlight
Before: 0 of 2 primitives give an instance-unique layoutId (21 importing files); behaviour not reproducible in jsdom
After: 2 of 2; a two-strip page keeps both highlights
Method: simulation - framer shared-layout projection does not run in jsdom, so the gate needs a browser render
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright page mounting two SubTabNavigation strips; assert both active pills visible after a click in the second

title: GenomeImportPanel: surface file-read failures and never stick in Decoding
body:
## Summary
The genome importer ignores FileReader errors and has no finally around decode/sanitize, so a failed read is silent and a throw leaves the panel busy.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_genome-share/GenomeImportPanel.tsx:113-118 sets reader.onload only; reader.onerror is unset, so an unreadable file yields no message. :76-78 setBusy(true) / await decodeBuildCode / setBusy(false) has no try/finally, and :97 calls the caller-supplied sanitize unguarded, so a sanitizer throw becomes an unhandled rejection from the click handler. Fixed: onerror sets an error line, try/finally around the busy window, a sanitize throw is reported as the error.

## Flow
- Import from File, choose a file the browser cannot read: nothing happens, no error
- a sanitize implementation throws: unhandled rejection, no message

## Expected impact
Item genome designers get a reason instead of silence. Risk: low, only error paths change.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every import failure reports its reason
Before: 0 of 2 failure paths (read error, sanitize throw) report anything
After: 2 of 2 render an error line
Method: simulation - walked the handlers; a FileReader-mock component test is the gate
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test mocking FileReader to fire onerror and a sanitize that throws; assert an error line renders and busy resets

title: Name the genome import textarea and build-code field
body:
## Summary
The build-code import textarea and the read-only build-code input have no accessible name; only a placeholder or value describes them.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_genome-share/GenomeImportPanel.tsx:145 <textarea> has placeholder only, no aria-label or <label>; src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_genome-share/BuildCodeExport.tsx:98 <input readOnly> likewise. A placeholder is not an accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2), so a screen reader announces an unnamed edit field. Fixed: aria-label on both.

## Flow
- open the item DNA genome Import panel with a screen reader
- focus the textarea: announced without a name

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users can find the import field. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - both fields are findable by role and name
Before: getByRole('textbox', {name: /build code/i}) matches 0 of 2 fields
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read the JSX; an RTL role query is the gate
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: RTL test: getByRole('textbox', {name}) for both fields

title: TimelineStrip says when it hides events past maxVisible
body:
## Summary
TimelineStrip slices events to maxVisible (50) and drops the rest with no indication.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_shared/dataviz.tsx:34 visible = events.slice(0, maxVisible), and the time range is computed from the visible slice only, so events 51+ vanish and the axis silently rescales. 3 consumers (EffectsTimelineSection, EventTimelinePanel, FeedbackTab). Fixed: a '+N more' marker when events.length > maxVisible.

## Flow
- pass 60 events
- observed: 50 drawn, nothing says 10 are hidden

## Expected impact
Designers reading a long effect or stagger timeline know it is truncated. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - truncation is visible
Before: 60 events: 0 indication of the 10 hidden
After: '+10 more' rendered
Method: simulation - read the slice; an RTL render with 60 events is the gate
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: RTL test rendering 60 events, assert '+10 more'

title: Pin init-prompt keys to the Feature Map section registry
body:
## Summary
INIT_PROMPTS is keyed by free strings, so a renamed section silently loses its scaffold prompt and grades no-prompt.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/feature-init-prompts.ts:22 types InitPromptMap as Record<string, FeatureInitPrompt>; feature-map-config.ts exports SectionId but the prompt maps do not use it, and no test compares the 68 prompt keys with getSections(). Measured today: 0 orphan keys, 5 sections with no prompt (combat damage-pipeline, attribute-defaults, encounter-choreography; inventory economy-sim, loot-filter). A rename in feature-map-config would make sectionScaffoldState return no-prompt with no failing gate. Fixed: a coverage test (keys subset of section ids per module, seeded red with a bogus key) or typing the maps with SectionId.

## Flow
- rename a section id in feature-map-config.ts
- observed: typecheck and tests stay green; the card loses its scaffold chip

## Expected impact
Keeps the scaffold panel honest as sections evolve. Risk: none, test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - prompt/section drift fails a gate
Before: 0 tests pin 68 keys
After: 1 test, seeded red by an orphan key
Method: probe - counted keys vs sections with a script over both files
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest coverage test over INIT_PROMPTS x getSections, with a seeded orphan to prove it bites

title: FeatureInitPrompt.label: 68 hand-written labels with no reader
body:
## Summary
Every init prompt carries a 'label' (button text) that nothing reads since FeatureInitButton was deleted.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/feature-init-prompts.ts:17 declares label 'Short action label for the button'; grep for getFeatureInitPrompt shows 3 readers (sectionScaffold.ts:39,58, useSectionScaffold.ts:61) that read only .prompt or existence. ScaffoldPanel builds its own 'Scaffold <section label>' text. Either delete the field (68 entries) or make it the panel's button text so the authored copy is used.

## Flow
- grep -rn getFeatureInitPrompt src: 3 readers, none reads .label

## Expected impact
Removes 68 unused copy strings or puts them on screen. Risk: low.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - dead data removed or used
Before: 68 labels, 0 readers
After: 0 dead labels
Method: probe - zero-reader grep over src
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: decide delete vs use; typecheck + section-scaffold tests as the gate

title: ScaffoldChip drops the run-failure reason on partial sections
body:
## Summary
The card chip shows the last run's failure reason only for absent sections; partial ones lose it, while the panel row shows it for both.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/ScaffoldPanel.tsx:20 partial gives 'missing X' with no v.reason; :21 absent gives v.reason. The panel row appends reason for both states. After a run that created one of two classes, the card says 'missing UARPGEncounterManager' and the row adds '(run finished, class not found)'. Fixed: the partial chip appends the reason like the row.

## Flow
- scaffold enemy-ai waves; the run creates only FARPGWaveConfig
- card chip: 'missing UARPGEncounterManager'; panel row: '... (run finished, class not found)'

## Expected impact
The card says why a section is still incomplete. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - chip and row agree on the reason
Before: 1 of 2 incomplete states carries the reason in the chip
After: 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read both renderers; the section-scaffold-hook harness can gate it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: section-scaffold-hook test: partial after a failed run, assert chip text includes the reason
